title: Ten Stories. One Mission.
excerpt: In May, we wrote that only 10 of every 100 Liberian children will ever finish primary school. This month, we made our first tuition payments. Here are the ten students who started the year fully paid.
body:
Our inaugural class: meet the 10 Dreamers you helped put in school

In May, we shared a stark reality: only 10 out of every 100 children born in Liberia will ever finish primary school. We said the system wouldn’t fix itself for that 10%. We also said it didn’t have to.

Last month, promise became reality. Ten incredible Dreamers in Monrovia walked through the doors of Samwa International Academy with their tuition paid in full.

This is their story—and the very first chapter of ours.

CECE’s first-ever Dreamers

Nine of our ten Dreamers are in junior or senior high school. That milestone matters deeply. According to the Ministry of Education’s most recent census, only 21% of junior-secondary-aged children and 17% of senior-secondary-aged children in Liberia are enrolled in school. Most young people their age have already been forced to leave their education behind.

These ten students refuse to give up on their futures—and our job, alongside our incredible community of Dream Makers, is to make sure cost is never the reason they have to.

Here are the bright minds walking into classrooms at Samwa International Academy this year because of your support:

  • Favor (age 11) – Grade 5
  • Success (age 14) – Grade 8
  • Ezekiel (age 20) – Grade 9
  • Lindsay (age 13) – Grade 10
  • Blessing (age 18) – Grade 10
  • Korpo (age 16) – Grade 10
  • Samuel (age 16) – Grade 11
  • Hawa (age 15) – Grade 12
  • Menileleh (age 15) – Grade 12
  • Ketrisha (age 17) – Grade 12

What your support covered

To ensure every Dreamer steps into the classroom with confidence, each student received a complete start-of-year package:

  • Full annual tuition, paid directly to Samwa International Academy
  • 2 uniform sets (standard school uniform + PE kit)
  • 2 pairs of shoes (black dress shoes + white sneakers)
  • 1 durable backpack
  • Essential supplies (notebooks, pens, math sets, lab coats)
  • 1 scientific calculator

We cover more than tuition on purpose. At most Liberian schools, uniforms and proper supplies are strictly required. A student who shows up without them stands out, falls behind, or gets sent home.

By taking care of everything from head to toe, Favor, Success, Ezekiel, Lindsay, Blessing, Korpo, Samuel, Hawa, Menileleh, and Ketrisha start on the exact same footing as every other child in the room. For their families, this kind of comprehensive support is the difference between staying in school and dropping out.

Supply pick-up day

In early September, our Dreamers and their families gathered to receive their materials. It was a beautiful moment of collective pride and readiness. They pulled on their CECE’s Dream shirts—as seen in our photos—and officially stepped into their roles as our inaugural class.

Some of our Dreamers beamed with wide, infectious smiles; others stood a bit tall and formal for the camera. But looking at them gathered together, you see ten young people who are ready, confident, and eager to learn.

What comes next

Paying tuition is just the beginning, and nowhere near our finish line.

Throughout the academic year, we’ll be conducting monthly check-ins to monitor attendance, track academic progress, and ensure our Dreamers have everything they need to thrive. We look forward to sharing their milestones and achievements directly with you.

And we aren't stopping at ten. Every new Dream Maker who joins our community means one more child inside a classroom instead of outside looking in.

Thank you to our Dream Makers

To our founding Dream Makers—Dwight E., Jason M., Jeff B., Jeremy T., Joseph P., Kolu Z., Nathan G., Onaolapo C., and our generous anonymous supporters—you gave when all we had was a vision. No track record, no photos, just a simple promise.

Now, that promise has ten names, ten bright futures, and ten stories in the making.

We also want to give a special thank-you to our dedicated volunteers, Kyle Bruxvoort and Tessa Chambers, whose time, talent, and energy behind the scenes helped bring our mission to life.

Finally, we want to recognize the visionary team behind CECE’s Dream: founder David Ziama, along with board members Peter Lazarz, Tera Palozola, Sandra Bruxvoort, Ashley Steyer, Jared Vanlandingham, Michael Taylor, and Jenny Waddle. Your dedication, leadership, and belief in these students made this milestone possible.

Thank you for helping us break barriers and build futures, one child at a time.

Sources

  • Liberia Education Statistics Report 2021-22 — Republic of Liberia Ministry of Education — junior and senior secondary enrollment figures

title: Nine Out of Ten
excerpt: Of every 100 children born in Liberia, only 10 will ever finish primary school. The number is shocking, but the reasons behind it are the more important story.
body:
Of every 100 children born in Liberia, only 10 will ever finish primary school. The number is shocking on its own. But the reasons behind it — and the path out — are the story we want to tell.

We've been asked, more than once, whether that statistic is real. It is. The figure comes from the official Annual School Census published by Liberia's Ministry of Education for 2021–22. It is the same source international donors and the World Bank rely on. And it is consistent with everything else we see in Liberia.

A country of children

Liberia's population is roughly 5.18 million. More than 40% of those people are of school-going age. Liberia is, demographically, a country of children. That share is not shrinking. It is expected to keep growing for the rest of this century.

This is the first thing to understand. The story of Liberian education is not a story about a small underserved minority. It is a story about a generation that includes a meaningful fraction of the entire country.

The funnel of attrition

Here is what happens to those children, level by level, according to the most recent census:

  • Only 46% of primary-school-aged children are enrolled in primary school. More than half of Liberia's youngest learners are missing from a classroom they should be in.
  • Only 21% of junior-secondary-aged children are enrolled in junior secondary. Four out of every five middle-school-aged children are not in middle school.
  • Only 17% of senior-secondary-aged children are enrolled in senior secondary. More than eight in ten high-school-aged kids are not in high school.
  • Only 10% of children ever finish even primary school.

Those numbers describe a system that is losing children at every gate.

The classroom they walk into

For the children who do make it inside, the conditions are not what most readers will recognize as a school.

In a Liberian high school, 32 students share a single math textbook. In some senior schools, that number reaches 65.

Only 8% of all schools in Liberia have piped drinking water. More than half rely on hand pumps. Some children still drink from creeks.

109 schools in Liberia can only be reached by canoe.

These are not edge cases. They are averages and counts from the national census.

Even when Liberian children make it to a classroom, the basics aren't there.

The economic reality

The reason most children are not in school is not a mystery. The average daily income in Liberia is $2.04 per person (World Bank, 2022). Tuition for a single school term, plus a uniform and a bag of textbooks, costs roughly what a typical family earns in two months.

Three crises within a single generation — civil war from 1989 to 2003, the Ebola outbreak from 2014 to 2016, and COVID from 2020 onward — closed schools for years at a time and pushed families into deeper poverty. When daily survival is the priority, school fees become an impossible luxury.

This is the part that does not show up in a single statistic. The 10% completion rate is not a story about children who chose to leave. It is a story about families forced to make the same hard choice, hundreds of thousands of times.

What we are doing about it

CECE's Dream is not trying to solve the entire system. We do one thing: we cover the cost of school for individual children, one at a time. Tuition, uniform, books, and a monthly check-in to make sure they are still showing up and learning.

A $50/month sponsorship covers the full cost of a Liberian student's school year. The system will not fix itself for the 10%. But it does not have to. The buildings are already standing. The teachers are already there. What's missing — for the average Liberian family — is the affordability of the seat.

Sponsor a student.

Sources

  • Liberia Education Statistics Report 2021-22 — Republic of Liberia Ministry of Education — primary source for enrollment, completion, textbook, water, and access figures
  • GDP per capita (current US$) — World Bank, Liberia — source for the $2.04/day daily income figure
  • Liberia: Trends in Completion Rates by Education Level and Gender — UNESCO IICBA — corroborates the primary completion rate
